text:
maya: Quick benchmarking question — we ran the same 70B quantized model on AWS (p4de), GCP (a2me-g8), and Azure (NDm A100) in eu-west and us-central. Results look... inconsistent. Anyone seen driver/CUDA stack cause 20-30% throughput differences before?
sam: yep, seen that. often CUDA + cuDNN version + kernel selection matters. what stack versions did you use?
maya: AWS: CUDA 11.7, driver 525.85, cuDNN 8.2. GCP: CUDA 12.2, driver 535.112, cuDNN 9.0. Azure: CUDA 11.8, driver 530.41, cuDNN 8.5.
diego: those are different major CUDA releases — that alone can change kernel codepaths and autotuned kernels. also NVLink topology differs across SKUs which affects multi-GPU batching.
jules: can you paste the perf command + model config? small seq len? batch size?
maya: sure — short snippet:
```
# runner flags
--model redwood/70b-qat8
--seq_len 2048
--batch 4
--quantize int8_dynamic
--warmup 100
--steps 500
--use_kv_cache true
```
sam: seq=2048 and batch=4 is latency sensitive. CUDA 12 builds have some attention kernels that target longer sequences better. that could explain lower p99 on GCP even if throughput lower.
maya: raw numbers (tokens/sec averaged over steady state): AWS p4de: 1850 tps, GCP a2me: 1420 tps, Azure NDm: 1650 tps. p95 latency: AWS 120ms, GCP 95ms, Azure 130ms.
diego: interesting — GCP lower throughput but best p95. might be that CUDA12 picked lower-latency kernels but with less batching efficiency. did you check kernel timings with nvprof / nsight?
maya: ran `nvprof --metrics achieved_occupancy` briefly. GCP shows lower occupancy on the big matmul kernels but much lower memcpy stalls. AWS is high occupancy but higher memcpy stalls.
infra-bot: deploy-check: all instances were pinned to the same CPU policy and isolated cpus?
maya: yes — `--cpuset-cpus 0-47` on all. hyperthreading off. same Docker image (sha: abc123) but built on different CUDA base images.
sam: another vector: driver bug/fix in 535.x improved small-batch GEMM performance in cuBLAS for Ampere->Hopper. also RMM/allocator behavior changed across CUDA versions which can affect fragmentation and memcpy behavior.
jules: did you try forcing kernels or fallback to older cublas/cuDNN to equalize? e.g. set `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`, or use `TF_FORCE_UNIFIED_MEMORY` equivalents?
maya: tried `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` and `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0` — marginal improvements on GCP only. swapping cuDNN to 8.5 on GCP (built locally) increased throughput by ~12% but p95 worsened.
diego: it smells like a kernel selection tradeoff: autotuner choosing smaller tile kernels (lower latency) vs larger batched kernels (higher throughput). For capacity sizing we should pick the kernel that matches our typical seq len distribution.
sam: Agreed. For production sizing we usually optimize for 95th percentile latency for chat workloads and throughput for batch embeddings. Which is the primary metric here?
maya: primary is throughput for streaming generation for customers (cost per token) but with a hard p95 SLA of <150ms.
jules: then AWS seems to hit throughput & p95 margin, GCP is great p95 but lower throughput -> higher cost. Azure in middle. Region placement also matters — eu-west AZ had slightly worse NUMA config and NVLink interconnects.
maya: we ran in eu-west-1 (aws), europe-west3 (gcp), and westeurope (azure).
diego: another thing: driver-level preemption and MIG-like behavior on multi-tenant hosts can impact. Are these multi-tenant or dedicated?
maya: these were dedicated / single-tenant SKUs (no multi-tenancy), except GCP a2me which is shared hardware in our project.
sam: recommendation: 1) pin CUDA/cuDNN combos and build identical runtime images per cloud, 2) rerun with a kernel-probe run to capture cuBLAS/cuDNN heuristics (trace logs), 3) compare warm vs cold caches, 4) run with `--batch 8` to see batching efficiency delta.
jules: also worth testing H100 developer images and cuFFT/cuBLAS patches if we move to Hopper. but for A100 class, ensure same driver major.
maya: follow-ups: I'll build a uniform runtime on CUDA 11.8 + cuDNN 8.5 (closest common denom) and rerun batch sweeps [1,2,4,8] and seq sweeps [512,1024,2048]. Will also capture `nvidia-smi topo -m`, `nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE`, and `nsys profile` flame for 50 steps.
diego: add `cuBLAS_log` env vars to dump chosen algorithms, and `CUDNN_LOGINFO_DBG=1` — helps explain heuristic choices.
sam: don't forget to record kernel versions and libcudnn.so symlink targets. tiny packaging differences cause different loaded libs.
maya: noted. I'll post results in this thread. Thanks all. :seedling:
maya: quick extra note later: for GCP the image used a distro with glibc 2.36 vs 2.34 on others — might affect libcallo performance on small memcpy loops. small but cumulative.
sam: ugh linux stack too. Good catch.
infra-bot: reminder: please attach config files and perf logs to the internal s3 bucket: s3://redwood-ml-bench/1710701234-gpu-crosscloud/
maya: uploaded raw logs + `nsys` traces + cuBLAS dumps. link: https://s3.redwood.internal/1710701234-gpu-crosscloud (internal)
jules: when you have the rerun, let's create a short note for the runbook: "Cross-cloud SKU parity checklist" — include CUDA/cuDNN versions, driver, distro, NVLink/PCIe topology, image sha, and capacity per-region guidance.
maya: will do. goal: recommend instance SKU + driver combo per region for lowest cost-per-token while meeting p95<150ms.
sam: if you want I can help synthesize the charts (latency/throughput vs batch/seq) once logs are in tableau.
maya: appreciate it. I'll ping again.
